# Native Passive-Load Readiness

This provisional F07 chapter accompanies child #11939 under #11791 and #11792.
It adds a necessary passive-load gate to the observations in
[Native Constrained-State Readiness](32-native-constrained-state.qmd), without
extending [Native Muscle Replay](13-native-muscle-replay.qmd) admission.
Passing declared limits never establishes anatomical or capture qualification.

## Native Evidence and Units

`tour_matching/native_passive_readiness.py` observes an owned native Model/State
through `audit_native_passive_readiness`. It supports exactly
`Thelen2003Muscle` and `Millard2012EquilibriumMuscle`, requires agreement between
recursive and registered muscle paths, and reuses the public constraint-state
observer for model/runtime/provider identities and outstanding state gates.
A State copy isolates realization caches; callers must prevent concurrent
Model mutation because lock targets can be model-owned. The observer neither
equilibrates nor integrates, assembles, unlocks, disables or overrides anything.

Lengths are metres, fiber velocity is metres per second, and forces are newtons.
Activation and excitation retain native dimensionless conventions. Native
`getPassiveFiberForce` is a fiber-axis quantity; tendon and fiber-along-tendon
forces are distinct outputs. Pennation projection must not be mistaken for
damping. The observed native maximum isometric force $F_{max}>0$ defines the
reported force ratios, not a universal physiological acceptance threshold.

For the admitted Millard law, the native passive fiber output combines elastic
and damping contributions:

$$F_{passive}=F_{elastic}+F_{damping},\qquad
r_{elastic}=F_{elastic}/F_{max},\qquad r_T=F_T/F_{max}.$$

The observer uses the actual `getPassiveFiberElasticForce` and
`getPassiveFiberDampingForce` accessors. The inspected
[Millard implementation](https://github.com/opensim-org/opensim-core/blob/85aaf64/OpenSim/Actuators/Millard2012EquilibriumMuscle.cpp)
computes these separately before their sum. The exact admitted
[Thelen implementation](https://github.com/opensim-org/opensim-core/blob/85aaf64/OpenSim/Actuators/Thelen2003Muscle.cpp)
has no parallel passive damping term: its passive fiber output is used as the
elastic contribution and the damping contribution is recorded as zero.
The runtime version names revision `85aaf64`; that string is not proof that
every installed binary or transitive library matches the inspected source.

Cancellation is a separate observation: the smaller absolute contribution when
elastic and damping terms have opposing signs, otherwise zero. It is not an
alternative to the elastic-force gate. Native fiber velocity also remains
visible; algebraic force balance does not imply a static prepared posture.

## Explicit Policy and Fail-Closed Admission

`PassiveReadinessPolicy` binds the loaded model SHA-256, declared preparation
scope and exactly one `MusclePassiveLimits` record per native muscle. Each record
requires source provenance, a positive finite normalized-fiber interval, finite
nonnegative elastic-force and tendon-force ratio limits, and explicit expected
activation-dynamics and tendon-compliance flags. No physiological limits are
invented by default. Provenance text is a declaration requiring external review,
not independent approval. The scope string does not execute or verify preparation.

The necessary tests are

$$\ell_{min}\leq\ell_f/\ell_{opt}\leq\ell_{max},\qquad
|r_{elastic}|\leq r_{elastic,max},\qquad |r_T|\leq r_{T,max}.$$

Missing policy, foreign model identity, incomplete or extra muscle coverage,
disabled/overridden muscles, changed runtime flags and violated limits block
`require_native_passive_readiness`. It obtains fresh native evidence instead of
accepting a caller-written receipt. Native option changes can leave the model
XML hash unchanged; they are checked independently. Nonfinite observations and
unsupported concrete laws cannot produce accepted evidence.

`within_declared_limits` describes only this necessary gate. The immutable
qualification field always reads `not-qualified-for-muscle-matching`, including
when synthetic permissive limits pass. The nested constraint audit preserves its
own blockers. Neither the observation digest nor an equilibrated state is a
complete-state artifact or authenticity certificate. Existing exploratory and
replay APIs are unchanged; future full-source matching orchestration must call
this gate and independently enforce anatomy, assistance, contact, complete state,
calibration, uncertainty and held-out validation requirements.

## Native Counterexamples and Source Findings

Both native-law fixtures equilibrate a 1 kg SliderJoint model at path length
0.32 m, activation 0.05, $F_{max}=1000$ N, optimal fiber length 0.1 m and tendon
slack length 0.1 m. Native fiber-along-tendon and tendon forces agree within
0.001 N while a deliberately synthetic elastic-force limit of 0.1 $F_{max}$
fails. These numbers test software rejection; they are not anatomical limits.

A separate nonsteady Millard fixture uses path length 0.25 m and explicitly
sets fiber length to 0.20 m after initial preparation. Native elastic force is
approximately 1857.14 N, damping is -1857.14 N, net passive force is approximately
zero, and fiber velocity is -18.57 m/s. A net-only check incorrectly accepted
this case before the regression; the elastic-force gate rejects it. No law or
anatomical parameter was changed to create acceptance.

The unchanged public 520-muscle source at commit
`3cfbe329a8ef9412494980419cb7177c41183a53`, source SHA-256
`a55c64341680551fb5a41be254bdfdb3b2be0ac789336ea44902b22fc9a83913`, was
evaluated with all 1348 previously prepared named values restored exactly and
native defaults for other state. No new equilibrium or source edit was performed.
All 520 muscles were observed, and the result remains `passive-policy-unavailable`.
MF_m5_laminar elastic force reaches 62.377 $F_{max}$; IL_L4 fiber-axis passive
force is 48406.73 N and its along-tendon/tendon force is 48066.55 N. These are
observed source-readiness concerns, not clinical safety limits or proof of an
anatomical defect. Missing visual meshes do not justify changing dynamics.

Exact torso donor release and assembly ancestry remain unavailable. The source's
torso citation alone does not identify a release checksum. Native reproduction
of endpoint/frame distances and minimum-activation equilibrium has not resolved
the loading. Obtain matching donor frame, endpoint, physiological parameter and
neutral-posture provenance before calibration or tuning; retain original failures.
Locked wrists, missing hand attachments, assistance, rigid tendons, ground/grip,
capture marker correspondence and full-state replay remain separate gates.

## Reproduction and Remaining Work

Run serially with the actual OpenSim runtime:

```text
python -m pytest tests/opensim/test_native_passive_readiness.py tests/opensim/test_native_constraint_state.py -o addopts='' -q
```

The native suite covers force-equilibrium rejection, damping cancellation,
runtime options, exact model/coverage, disabled/overridden drives, finite limits,
missing provenance and immutable unqualified results. Default Python without
OpenSim skips native cases and supplies no native evidence. The local full-source
receipt retains source/preparation/runtime/provider hashes, all observed muscles
and constraint blockers; it contains no private capture and is not a committed
foreign model. Physiological policy approval, exact donor comparison, whole-model
matching and independent full-horizon replay remain outstanding. Manual rendering,
page review and publication approval remain governed and blocked.
